task.description: SECURITY-REVIEWER hard gate (WF-02 Step 2c) on REQ-162's implementation, commit e937135 on lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex. This requirement's own text explicitly names SECURITY-REVIEWER as a hard gate because a SCRIPT_ERROR's stack trace and message are a data-disclosure surface -- a script author's error view must never leak host filesystem paths, Elixir module internals, other tenants' data, or capability grants beyond what that script's own execution held. ELIXIR-DEV made build_script_error/3 public (marked @doc false) as a deliberate test seam -- verify this does not create an unintended public API surface or a new way to invoke error-shaping logic outside its intended call site. Read the approved design (lib/letflow/design/req162-lua-script-error-capture.md) and the real diff (git show e937135 -- lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex) in full before verdict.
acceptance_criteria: Confirm the typed-case stack trace (Lua.RuntimeException.to_map(exception).call_stack) genuinely cannot contain an Elixir module atom, a BEAM stacktrace frame, or a real host filesystem path -- verify by reading the real vendored source path that constructs it, not just trusting the design's structural-guarantee argument.
Confirm the untyped/fallback case's fixed placeholder message and empty stack_trace genuinely discard the original exception's message/details rather than partially leaking them.
Confirm the capabilities field only ever reflects the CURRENT script execution's own grant set -- never another tenant's, another script's, or a superset/host-internal capability list.

Confirm build_script_error/3 being made public (test seam) does not introduce a new caller-reachable code path that could be invoked with attacker-controlled or cross-tenant data from somewhere other than run_script/3's own rescue clause.
Confirm no new Letflow.Repo call or tenant-prefix-derivation was introduced anywhere in this diff.
Confirm the instruction_count two-tag union cannot be manipulated by a script to fabricate a false 'consumed' vs 'configured_budget' signal.
Cross-check against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md INV-1..INV-8 explicitly, naming which apply and confirming each holds.
CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field (line 9) must be exactly PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish -- run mix letflow.lint_handoffs before finishing.

result.summary: SECURITY-REVIEWER verdict on commit e937135 (executor.ex): PASS. All 8 acceptance criteria verified against the actual committed code and the real vendored deps/lua source, not just the design doc's argument.
findings: AC1 (typed-case stack trace cannot leak Elixir/host detail): confirmed by reading deps/lua/lib/lua/runtime_exception.ex (to_map/2 dispatches to RuntimeError.to_map/2, TypeError.to_map/2, or AssertionError.to_map/2 for those three struct shapes -- exactly the set executor.ex's script_error_stack_trace/1 typed-case guard matches), deps/lua/lib/lua/vm/error_formatter.ex (to_map/3 -> build_call_stack/1 builds frames solely from Executor.frame_source/1, frame_line/1, frame_name/1), and deps/lua/lib/lua/vm/executor.ex (frame_source/frame_line/frame_name read only {source, line, hint} tuples or maps pushed onto state.call_stack at Lua call sites -- never __STACKTRACE__, never an Elixir module atom, never Process.info). executor.ex's own run_script/3 calls Lua.eval!(lua, script_source) with no :source option, so source defaults to the literal '<eval>' (deps/lua/lib/lua.ex line 529 Keyword.validate! default), never a real filesystem path. Structural guarantee holds: build_call_stack/1 has no code path that reads an Elixir module or a host path in the first place.

AC2 (untyped/fallback fully discards message/stacktrace): confirmed. script_error_message/1's fallback clause (executor.ex line 472) returns the fixed @script_error_placeholder_message constant unconditionally for any Lua.RuntimeException whose .original is not RuntimeError/TypeError/AssertionError -- it never touches Exception.message(exception) or exception.original at all. script_error_stack_trace/1's fallback clause (line 480) returns a bare [] the same way. No partial leak: both clauses are total discards, not a scrub of the original value.

AC3 (capabilities field reflects only the current execution's own grant set): confirmed. run_script/3's rescue clause passes Capabilities.new() (a freshly-constructed empty MapSet, not a shared/cached value) directly into build_script_error/3 at the call site (line 417), and build_script_error/3 renders it via MapSet.to_list/1 with no other data source. Capabilities.new/0,1 (capabilities.ex) is pure and stateless -- no process dictionary, no ETS, no cross-call memoization -- so there is no code path by which one execution's capabilities value could carry another execution's or another tenant's grants. The field is empty today only because of the pre-existing, disclosed OQ-1 wiring gap (Sandbox.new/1 always installs Capabilities.new()), not because of any cross-execution leak.

AC4 (build_script_error/3 as a public @doc false test seam does not add a new attacker-reachable path): confirmed. It requires a genuine %Lua.RuntimeException{} struct as its first argument -- there is no way to construct or forge one from outside deps/lua's own exception/1 clauses (defexception's struct-literal syntax is available to any caller technically, but Elixir module boundaries do not create a privilege distinction here: any caller that could construct a fake %Lua.RuntimeException{} could equally have called this function before it existed, e.g. via Exception.message/1 or to_map/2 directly on a hand-built struct -- REQ-162 does not change what an Elixir-level caller could already do). The function does no I/O, no lookup, no side effect -- it is a pure map-shaping function over its three arguments. Not part of the Executor behaviour, not called from any router/plug/controller, not reachable from Lua script code itself (Lua scripts cannot call arbitrary Elixir functions outside the gated platform.* surface). Its only real callers are run_script/3's own rescue clause and executor_test.exs.

AC5 (no new Repo calls or tenant-prefix derivation): confirmed by grep -- zero Letflow.Repo references anywhere in executor.ex; the only 'tenant' occurrence in the file is a moduledoc prose sentence ('it executes tenant-supplied script source directly'), not code. The diff (git show e937135) touches no Ecto/Repo code at all.

AC6 (instruction_count two-tag union cannot be manipulated by a script to fabricate a false signal): confirmed. instruction_count_report/2 pattern-matches on exception.original's own :state field (%{state: %Lua.VM.State{instruction_count: count}} -> {:consumed, count}; anything else -> {:configured_budget, budget}). This value is populated entirely by the VM's own raise sites in deps/lua/lib/lua/vm/executor.ex (confirmed: RuntimeError/TypeError/AssertionError raises pass state: state, i.e. the VM's own internal counter snapshot at the instant of the raise) -- a Lua script has no host function, global, or platform.* capability that can set, overwrite, or spoof exception.original.state; it is Elixir-side VM bookkeeping never exposed to the Lua sandbox. A script cannot fabricate a %Lua.VM.State{} value from Lua code, and cannot avoid triggering the real one when it raises via a genuine VM opcode.
INV-1 (tenant data isolation): NOT-APPLICABLE. No Ecto schema, no migration, no business-data table, no Repo call anywhere in this diff -- confirmed by grep (AC5 finding).
INV-2 (server-side field authorisation): NOT-APPLICABLE per file's own applicability note -- S4 API surface not started; also this change touches no API response/controller/view path.

INV-3 (untrusted runtime sandboxing): APPLIES (S5 scripting is in progress -- REQ-162 is itself an S5 Lua-scripting requirement) and HOLDS. This diff is purely additive to the existing sandbox's error-reporting path; it introduces no new host function, no new capability-bypass path, and no ambient network/filesystem access. It reads only pre-existing sandbox state (the grant set already installed by Sandbox.new/1) and pre-existing VM exception structs -- it does not touch capabilities.ex, platform.ex, or sandbox.ex's gating logic at all (confirmed: diff is scoped entirely to executor.ex).

INV-4 (secrets by reference only): NOT-APPLICABLE. No secret material (API keys, tokens, DB URLs) is read, logged, or threaded through any value in this diff -- script_error's fields are all Lua-VM-internal or execution-local values (message, stack frames, instruction count, capability strings), none of which are secrets per this invariant's definition.
INV-5 (not-found/forbidden indistinguishability): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no lookup-by-ID endpoint exists in this diff; S4 not started.

INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping): NOT-APPLICABLE as a data-access-path invariant -- this diff introduces no new data-access path (no Repo query, no new host function). This handoff itself is SECURITY-REVIEWER's own proof artifact per this meta-invariant's own mechanism.
INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no SQL, no Repo.query anywhere in this diff (confirmed by the same grep as AC5/INV-1).

INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths): APPLIES (this diff's whole purpose is error handling on tenant-controlled Lua script input) and HOLDS. The new code is entirely pattern-matched with total function clauses across all reachable input shapes: script_error_message/1 and script_error_stack_trace/1 each have an exhaustive two-clause total match (typed struct guard, then a catch-all %Lua.RuntimeException{} clause) with no case that can fail to match a real Lua.RuntimeException; instruction_count_report/2's catch-all _original clause makes it total over any term(). No bare pattern match that can raise on realistic (attacker-supplied Lua script) input was introduced. Verified: mix compile --warnings-as-errors clean and full mix test 2283 passed / 0 failures per the implementation commit's own message -- consistent with no unhandled-crash regression.
Design-vs-implementation cross-check: build_script_error/3's real code matches design §3/§6/§13 exactly -- no divergence found between the approved design doc and the committed diff.
